To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) statins have a protective effect on the cardiovascular system, which is independent from cholesterol lowering; (b) statins exert a protective effect on atherosclerosis and on the cardiovascular system by reducing vascular inflammation; and (c) statins have pleiotropic effects on vascular cells, which include a direct effect on vascular smooth muscle cells, endothelial cells and macrophages, and a direct and an indirect effect on platelets

(1) statins are not only lipid-lowering drugs but are also anti-inflammatory agents that improve endothelial function and reduce vascular inflammation and oxidative stress, (2) the anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects of statins are not limited to the vascular system, but extend to the entire organism, (3) statin discontinuation, or statin “withdrawal” syndrome, is associated with rebound deterioration of endothelial function, increased vascular inflammation and oxidative damage, and worse cardiovascular outcomes

statin withdrawal or “statin rebound” is a real phenomenon, and that it is associated with a deterioration in vascular function, which can be detrimental in patients undergoing major surgery and in those with a stroke or myocardial infarct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of statin withdrawal on endothelial and platelet function, as well as the effects of statins on endothelial progenitor cells (EPC) and their role in atherogenesis and vascular repair.
the effects of statin discontinuation in patients admitted for acute coronary syndromes, acute ischemic stroke, and after major vascular surgery.
the effects of statins on the cardiovascular system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive evidence that statin discontinuations are associated with an adverse clinical outcome.
in the presence of a vascular crisis, statin discontinuation is associated with a rebound or withdrawal syndrome, which may be life-threatening.
the risk of statin discontinuation in the setting of acute ischemic stroke or major vascular surgery is not yet known.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
statin rebound or withdrawal syndrome does exist, but only under specific conditions of severe acute stress.
statin withdrawal or rebound is not a myth, and the clinical consequences are potentially severe.
statins are a class of drugs with pleiotropic effects on the vascular system, and that the benefits and risks of statins depend on the context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
statins are not just cholesterol-lowering agents.
the risk of adverse outcomes is increased when statins are removed during a period of acute vascular stress, but not during stable conditions.
statins must be continued in patients with acute vascular syndromes, including those with acute coronary syndromes, stroke, and unstable angina.
